subject: POC environment preflight and close plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC environment preflight and proposed close plan

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, I pulled together a short preflight checklist and a proposed close timeline so your infra team can validate we meet your gating criteria before the pilot cutover. High-level items we need to complete in the MAP for the POC: 

- Org & user setup: create Nebula Health org in our Console and add 2 service accounts
- API keys: generate scoped API keys for the POC (read/generate tokens, no billing admin)
- IP allowlist: add Nebula outbound CIDRs (we'll provide an allowlist CSV)
- VPC peering: exchange peering info and schedule the peering test window

Attached: redwood_map_v3.xlsx (MAP draft) and network_allowlist.csv (example).

Proposed schedule:
- Day 0 (Mon 12/08): Org + API keys created
- Day 1 (Tue 12/09): IP allowlist applied and connectivity smoke tests
- Day 2 (Wed 12/10): VPC peering handshake & RTT tests
- Day 4 (Fri 12/12): Canary traffic + acceptance sign-off

Can you confirm: 1) whether your ops team prefers the peering window on Tue 12/09 or Wed 12/10, and 2) the best contact email for firewall/infra changes?

If that works I can convert the MAP into a mutually-signed milestone plan and loop in our legal for the order form.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@nebulahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@nebulahealth.com
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC environment preflight and proposed close plan

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear plan. Ops is available but we need a slightly wider maintenance window for the allowlist change — can we do Wednesday 12/10 for the IP allowlist (so we have time to validate egress patterns)? Also, a quick question on peering: does Redwood absorb NAT gateway costs for the peering test, or should we budget for an hourly cost on our side?

Primary infra contact for firewall work is: ops@nebulahealth.com (they monitor the ticketing queue). If you can share the exact CIDR file and a minimal port list, that will speed things up.

Happy to sign the MAP once dates are locked. We may want a 48-hour canary rather than single-day canary given transaction volume.

Thanks —
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform, Nebula Health
Samantha.Lee@nebulahealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 13:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: POC environment preflight and proposed close plan

Samantha — thanks, that all makes sense. Quick answers: 

- IP allowlist: we can move the allowlist change to Wed 12/10 — noted.
- Peering cost: Redwood covers the peering test window (first 4 hours) for POCs; longer-term egress during production is billed per the contract. I'll note that in the MAP.
- Canary length: 48-hour canary is fine; we'll add a rollback gate at 24 hours in case of any regression.

Action owners (internal):
- Org & API keys: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
- Networking & peering coordination: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
- MAP doc + order form: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

I attached a small how-to for scoped API key creation (vpc_peering_steps.docx) and updated the MAP sheet (redwood_map_v3.xlsx) with the 48-hour canary option. Next steps from our side: generate the two service account keys and post them to a secure Share link (we'll share the link to ops@nebulahealth.com).

I'll schedule a 30-min alignment call for Mon 12/08 10:00 PT unless you'd prefer a different slot.

—Jonas

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 09:45:00 -08:00

Forwarding a short technical checklist for your infra team — see inline and attached network_allowlist.csv.

----- Forwarded message from Grace O'Connor -----
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Technical preflight checklist (CIDRs/ports/service account)

Samantha / Ops team —

Quick checklist to get the peering and allowlist validated: 
- CIDR ranges we will announce: 34.120.0.0/16, 34.121.128.0/18 (please validate no overlap with Nebula private networks)
- Ports: 443 outbound (TLS), 5222 for internal websocket fallback (optional)
- Service account: create SA named redwood-poc-sa with roles: compute.viewer, network.viewer, secretmanager.accessor
- Expected test traffic: token-generation + small inference calls (~5RPS average for canary)

Attachments: network_allowlist.csv (CSV of our IPs), vpc_peering_steps.docx (peering checklist).

Let me know if you need an RFC1918 mapping or a separate test VLAN for the smoke tests.

—Grace
Staff Engineer, Infra
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@nebulahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@nebulahealth.com
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: POC environment preflight and proposed close plan

Thanks — that checklist is perfect. Ops confirmed the CIDRs do not overlap and they've queued the firewall change for Wed 12/10 03:00–05:00 PT. Peering test booked for Thu 12/11 07:00–09:00 PT.

We are ok with the 48-hour canary (12/12 00:00 PT through 12/14 00:00 PT). Please send the MAP for signature and a PO/DocuSign if possible — our procurement team prefers a DocuSign flow. Also: please send the secure link for the API keys when ready; ops will retrieve them and rotate after the canary.

Samantha
Head of Platform, Nebula Health
